sections.what: The clinic serves uninsured adults of McHenry County on a sliding fee scale without turning away inability to pay. It does not accept health insurance. Whole recipient scope includes Pink Door thrift operations and care/navigation.
sections.monitoring: FY2025 annual report counts 6,093 patient visits, 626 therapy sessions and 12,437 prescriptions. Use visits × 0.25 as a judged distinct clinically meaningful episode proxy; do not add therapy or medication counts. Reported control rates (67% diabetes, 84% hypertension) are cross-sectional, not causal gains relative to similar untreated people. Request deduplicated patients, baseline and follow-up symptoms/function, medication persistence and alternatives. The episode fraction is an assumption, not observed deduplication, and assumes nonoverlapping person-time health gains.
sections.qualitative: New staff and five additional volunteer doctors in the annual report suggest capacity can change, without proving gift elasticity. Medical and dental care can relieve illness; Oregon insurance trial cautions against translating access mechanically into physical health. Mortality and other net health set zero; nonhealth value remains outside QALYs.
sections.cost: Original FY2025 Form 990 p10 expense $2,393,158 excludes $86,349 donated services and $58,975 event costs, reconciled on Schedule D p25 to audited expense $2,538,482. Add $100,874 inventory cost netted on p9 for whole-recipient $2,639,356. This prudently restores thrift goods cost; direct audit still needed to confirm its presentation. Model 6,093 × 0.25 distinct episodes × 0.3 additional clinical response × 0.05 utility × 0.5 year × 0.35 funding capacity × 0.98 MSA share.
sections.funding: The original return reports $1,387,765 government grants and $5,575,072 ending net assets. This conflicts with annual-report wording that operations do not rely on government funding; use filed numbers and do not claim independence. Donated services are included once; externally provided medicines/tests beyond recorded accounts remain unpriced. No priced unfunded expansion found. Whole-recipient costs are retained regardless of donor restriction.

model.costScope: Full filed expense plus netted events/inventory and donated services from original Schedule D; external-care sensitivity adds assumed $1m, not an observed estimate.
model.counterfactual: a removes equivalent care elsewhere and ineffective care; b separately removes replacement financing/volunteer capacity. One morbidity pathway avoids double counting.
model.geographicAttribution: McHenry uninsured adult mission; .98 allows unmeasured mobility/residency leakage; excludes Kenosha and other non-MSA counties.
model.uncertainty: Central illustrative scenario and favorable/poor bounds are judgments, not calibrated EV or confidence interval. Cross-recipient results cannot be summed without deduplication. These costs are whole-portfolio equivalents, not marginal gift purchase guarantees. Cost numerators use different accounting recognition of donated care; central prices must not be interpreted as a comparable economic-efficiency ranking. Favorable and poor scenarios are illustrative cases, not exhaustive bounds.
